rootUpdate.currentStateSummary: Accepted work now includes an exact finite-block code-induced dependence-balance condition and a finite-entropic no-go result for one specified coarse entropy and copy-lemma refinement. Neither result establishes the BSSC sum-capacity.
rootUpdate.localResidualSummary: Coordinate the code-induced converse route with independent achievability and converse work. The coarse entropy/copy obstruction leaves structure-preserving reductions, binary-posterior constraints, and other channel-specific refinements unresolved.

intermediateResults.title: Finite entropic witness obstructing the specified entropy/copy refinement
intermediateResults.statement: An actual finite entropic witness satisfies the stated coarse BSSC relaxation and attains both direct sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4, so universally valid finite-variable information inequalities and every finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions cannot lower that specified relaxation below this value.
scopeQualifications: Exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints may exclude the witness and remain viable.
The conclusion obstructs only the specified coarse entropy, universal-information-inequality, and finite standard copy-lemma relaxation; it is not a broadcast-channel capacity bound.
The finite witness is not itself an actual binary-input BSSC distribution.

proofs: An explicit independent-component finite distribution satisfies the stated relaxation and objective exactly.
Conditional-resampling realizes every finite standard copy-lemma extension while preserving the original witness marginal and objective.
methods: Exact affine-in-h component-entropy audit and analytic tangent verification of the scalar posterior-support inequalities.
computations: Exact symbolic verification of structural equalities, dependence balance, conditional BEC identities, support rows, and both objective branches.

intermediateResults.title: Finite-block code-induced dependence balance and compatible rate rows
intermediateResults.statement: Every deterministic private-message code induces an exact finite-block dependence-balance identity, a fixed-coordinate encoder-map factorization, and four compatible Fano-adjusted rate bounds after uniform-time single-letterization.
scopeQualifications: The message alphabets and the alphabet of W may grow with blocklength, so this is not itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
The result is an exact sequence-level necessary condition for deterministic private-message codes, not by itself a broadcast-channel capacity bound.

proofs: Exact endpoint-replacement telescope, separate receiver Fano bounds, and chain-rule derivations of all four rate rows.
methods: Uniform-time single-letterization retaining the complete fixed-coordinate encoder-map factorization.
